candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register družb za izdajo elektronskega denarja (EMI register)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative national register of licensed e-money institutions, their agents and branches; the definitive list of licensed non-bank competitors (e.g. Paywiser) and of entries/deletions signalling market entry and exit.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML/PDF fetch of register pages plus change-notification list; diff entity list run-over-run.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for regulator register terms

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije – Plačilne institucije držav EGP v Sloveniji (EEA passporting-in list)

brief: Slovenia's non-bank payments competition is unusually well documented at the licensing layer: Banka Slovenije's EMI and EEA-passporting registers give an authoritative, diffable universe of local and cross-border PSPs/EMIs, with Paywiser as the flagship domestic licensed EMI. The commercial layer is thin and fragmented — vendor sites (mBills, VALÚ, Paywiser, Eligma/GoCrypto, Bankart/Flik) plus telco press releases carry most partnership and KPI disclosure, since the largest acquirer (Nexi) appears to have no Slovenian newsroom and speaks only through the group and partner banks. Local-language trade and business media (Monitor, Računalniške novice, Forbes Slovenija, Delo) are the practical discovery channel for market entries and merchant tie-ups that English sources never report, and community forums add weak-signal detail on acceptance friction. Priority follow-ups are the gov.si virtual-currency provider register, vendor developer/integration documentation, and clarifying the conflicting signals about mBills' continued operation.
